title: Picking a word out by position
idea: Indexing works the same for a list of words. The index gives back one word. Mixes review of strings and print.

exercises.explanation: Index 0 is the first word, "Mon". When you print a single word from a list, the quotes are not shown — just the text Mon.
Positions: Ada at 0, Grace at 1, Alan at 2. So names[2] gives the third name, Alan.

exercises.prompt: Indexing a list of words follows the same 0-based rule as a list of numbers.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Whether the values are numbers or words, the first is at index 0. The rule does not change with the kind of value.

exercises.prompt:
Note the difference. Predict the output:

colors = ["red", "green"]
print(colors)
exercises.explanation: Printing the WHOLE list shows brackets and quotes: ['red', 'green']. Only when you index ONE word do you get bare text.
colors[0] is the single word "red". Printing one string shows just its text: red, with no brackets or quotes.

exercises.prompt: For fruits = ["apple", "pear", "plum"], match each index to its word.
exercises.explanation: apple is first (0), pear is second (1), and -1 reaches the last word, plum.

exercises.prompt:
Complete the line to print the SECOND name:

names = ["Sam", "Lee", "Kai"]
print(names[____])
exercises.explanation: The second name is at index 1 (Lee). The first, Sam, would be index 0.

exercises.prompt:
You can join an indexed word to other text with +. Predict the output:

names = ["Ada", "Grace"]
print("Hi " + names[0])
exercises.explanation: names[0] is "Ada", and "Hi " + "Ada" joins to "Hi Ada". An indexed word behaves just like any string.

exercises.prompt: A word pulled from a list can be used in string joining, just like any other string.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Indexing gives back an ordinary string, so you can join it with + or use it anywhere a string fits.

exercises.prompt: A menu = ["soup", "salad", "pasta"]. Which line greets with today's special (the first item)?
exercises.explanation: menu[0] is "soup", and joining gives "Today: soup". Indexing picks the first item; printing the whole menu would show the brackets.
